page.overview:
Who is Crane?

Crane was a human female princess. Orphaned and exiled following the destruction of her kingdom by the Empire, she later became an operative for the Rebellion. Her childhood guardian was the astromech droid Tor-Tu, who remained her companion and partner in the Rebellion. He could transform into mechanical armor that allowed Crane to fly. While stationed at a secret rebel base on the planet Joetz, Crane and Tor-Tu tracked Imperial operations in the area. While conducting a reconnaissance mission, the pair rescued Woopas, the only survivor of an Imperial attack on a village in the planet's polar region. When they encountered an enormous Imperial mining crawler and its walker escorts, Crane had Tor-Tu engage his armor mode, which allowed her to destroy the entire force and end the Imperial occupation of the planet.

Crane was a princess of the Kingdom of Biwaji, where she lived with her mother. When she was just a child, the Empire attacked and destroyed the kingdom. As fires blazed up all around them, her mother told Crane to escape without her. She told the droid Tor-Tu to take care of her daughter, then stayed behind to await her fate. Crane never saw her again.

When Crane was older, she joined the Rebellion against the Empire. She was with the Rebels at their hidden base on the planet Joetz. An Imperial force landed in a snowy polar region of the planet. The base's commander, Admiral Kiucee, sent Crane on a reconnaissance mission to scout out the Empire's activities and determine whether the Rebels had been discovered. Crane drove out in a speeder bike with Tor-Tu riding along in the sidecar. On the way, Admiral Kiucee warned Crane not to make too much noise; she should keep her engine quiet and refrain from playing music in Tor-Tu's record cube feature. Crane played her music anyway. She also corrected the admiral when he addressed her as "Princess:" the kingdom was gone, she argued, and it was better to leave it in the past.

Crane and Tor-Tu came upon a ruined village, which she concluded must have been destroyed by the Empire. Under the floor of a house, they found Woopas, a tiny Gigoran child cowering in fear amidst four-winged paper cranes that he had made. Crane recognized them as representations of his people's guardian deity. She persuaded the child to trust her and follow her to safety. Outside, the three fought their way past a patrol of Imperial Snowtroopers and escaped in the speeder bike. Out on the frozen plain, they discovered an enormous Imperial mining crawler. Tor-Tu scanned the monstrosity and determined that the Empire was using it to mine the valuable hyperfuel coaxium. Realizing that the Imperials had come to Joetz to extract the mineral, not hunt for the Rebels, Crane reported back to Admiral Kiucee.
